# Distinguish selecting a destination from exporting its bytes

## Platform difference

An OH picker result or an app-private output path is not by itself a completed, user-accessible export.

## Implementation

PixEz replaces Android SAF operations with OH picker read/write APIs. Pica Comic adds a native download-directory bridge and conditional migration from its earlier private download location, and imports scripts from picker paths/bytes. ConnSSH stages a download, invokes a save operation with bytes, attempts a destination write and preserves its temporary copy on failure/cancellation. Neon accepts data in its OH save interface but does not pass or write those bytes in the inspected implementation. Draftmark creates a PDF in its private export directory and displays the path; Zhiji similarly returns direct-file export paths. Those latter flows require a separate user-delivery acceptance decision.

## Applicability

Choose among private persistence, imported copy, user-selected export and system sharing explicitly. Preserve the app-facing save method contract across platforms.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

ConnSSH buffers whole files, rejects batch download in its current OH path and mishandles empty byte arrays as failures; these are app tradeoffs, not filesystem laws. A returned URI is not necessarily suitable for File(path). PixEz first removes every dot from filenames and later restores the final extension dot: this is application sanitization policy, not proof that OH globally forbids dots.

## Verification

Export nonempty and zero-byte files, cancel the picker, fail a write, inspect the destination from another app, and test large files without assuming the staged copy is the final export.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.
